name: Human Body
facts: Your body has about 206 bones as an adult, but babies are born with around 300 that later fuse.
The smallest bone in your body is the stapes, in your middle ear.
Your heart beats around 100,000 times a day.
Your stomach makes a new layer of mucus constantly so that its own acid doesn't digest it.
Your ears and nose keep growing slowly throughout your life, because cartilage keeps changing shape with age.
Smell is closely linked to memory, because smell signals travel to brain areas involved in emotion and memory.
The human brain uses about 20% of the body's energy, though it is only about 2% of body weight.
Fingernails grow two to three times faster than toenails.
Your heart pumps around 7,000 litres of blood a day.
The cornea is one of the only parts of the body with no blood supply; it gets oxygen straight from the air.
You are slightly taller in the morning than at night, because the discs in your spine compress during the day.
Your skin is your body's largest organ.
Babies are born without kneecaps made of bone; they start as cartilage and harden over years.
Muscles make up around a third or more of an adult's body weight.
Humans are the only animals known to blush.
Identical twins have different fingerprints.
The femur, your thigh bone, is the longest and strongest bone in your body.
A single red blood cell lives for about 120 days.
Your eyes blink around 15 to 20 times a minute.
Adults have 32 teeth, including wisdom teeth.
Your liver can regrow to full size even after a large part of it is removed.
The small intestine is about 6 metres long in an adult.
Your body has more bacterial cells than you might think: roughly as many as your own human cells.
Goosebumps are a leftover reflex from ancestors who puffed up their body hair to keep warm or look bigger.
Taste buds are replaced roughly every one to two weeks.
